title: Soil Sampling and Preparation for Soil Chemical Analysis
author: Matema LE Imakumbili
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x72frqe

steps.title: Determine Sampling Strategy
steps.instruction: Observe the field for gradients or slopes to select the appropriate sampling design.

substeps.instruction: For relatively even fields: randomly select 10 to 20 sampling points.
For large fields with an obvious slope: select sampling points along the slope in one straight line.
Alternatively, use a grid sampling design (orderly version of random) or a zigzag sampling design for large uneven fields.
Avoid sampling depressions or field edges.

steps.title: Collect Soil Sub-samples
steps.instruction: Collect soil sub-samples from each selected point and aggregate them in a bucket.

substeps.instruction: Remove surface litter using a hoe or spade.
Cut a thin slice of soil (approximately 5 cm thick) from a depth of 0-20 cm (from surface to 20 cm below).
Ensure an equal quantity of soil is collected from the top to the bottom of the 0-20 cm depth.
Place the slice in the bucket; a soil sampler or auger may be used to facilitate collection.
Repeat for all planned sampling points.

steps.title: Prepare Composite Sample
steps.instruction: Create a representative composite sample from the bulk soil in the bucket.

substeps.instruction: Thoroughly mix the bulk sample by hand.
Use a 300-500 g plastic cup or bowl to collect a 300-500 g soil sample from the mixed bulk soil.

steps.title: Label and Transport Sample
steps.instruction: Secure the sample in a labeled container for transport to the laboratory.

substeps.instruction: Place the collected soil sample in a plastic bag.
Label the outside of the bag.
Place a small labeled paper with the field's name inside the bag for verification.

steps.title: Air-Dry Soil
steps.instruction: Dry the soil at room temperature in a dust-free, well-ventilated room.

substeps.instruction: Spread the soil on ink-free paper or a plastic sheet.
Maintain a temperature between 25°C and 35°C.
Ensure samples are separated to prevent cross-contamination.
Allow the soil to air-dry for approximately 1 to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Sieve and Store Soil
steps.instruction: Process the dried soil to remove debris and prepare it for chemical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Sieve the dry soil using a 2 mm sieve to remove stones and large pieces of plant litter.
Pack the resulting fine soil in a well-labeled plastic bag.
